report:
<report>
The evidence does not support the view that CoQ10 improves movement symptoms in Parkinson's disease. Early small trials, notably Shults et al. (2002, Arch Neurol), suggested that high-dose CoQ10 (1200 mg/day) slowed functional decline measured by the UPDRS, generating optimism that it might be neuroprotective. However, these findings were not confirmed in larger, more rigorous studies.

The pivotal QE3 trial—a large, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study testing 1200 mg and 2400 mg/day of CoQ10 in early PD—was halted for futility after an interim analysis showed no difference between CoQ10 and placebo in UPDRS progression, and the trial was formally reported as negative (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3975832/).

Subsequent systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials have reinforced this conclusion. One meta-analysis found that CoQ10 produced only nonsignificant improvement across UPDRS subscores compared with placebo (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10072-016-2757-9). Another systematic review and meta-analysis concluded plainly that "CoQ10 supplementation does not slow functional decline nor provide any symptomatic benefit for patients with Parkinson's disease" (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281460312_Coenzyme_Q10_for_Patients_with_Parkinson's_Disease_A_Systematic_Review_and_Meta-Analysis). A broader 2022 systematic review of CoQ10 in parkinsonian syndromes similarly found that while CoQ10 levels are reduced in PD tissues (supporting a biological rationale), clinical trial evidence for symptomatic or disease-modifying benefit remains weak and inconsistent (https://www.mdpi.com/2075-4426/12/6/975).

CoQ10 does appear safe and well tolerated even at high doses, but safety is not the same as efficacy.

Conclusion: The best current evidence, especially from the large QE3 trial and subsequent meta-analyses, indicates that CoQ10 does NOT meaningfully improve movement disorders in Parkinson's disease, contradicting the initial hypothesis.
</report>
